In mathematics, specifically in [[category theory]] and [[algebraic topology]], the '''Baez–Dolan stabilization hypothesis''', proposed in {{harv|Baez|Dolan|1995}}, states that [[suspension (topology)|suspension]] of a [[weak n-category|weak ''n''-category]] has no more essential effect after ''n'' + 2 times.<ref>{{cite arXiv|last=Lurie|first=Jacob|author-link=Jacob Lurie|date=2009-10-30|title=Derived Algebraic Geometry VI: E_k Algebras|eprint=0911.0018|language=en|at=Example 1.2.3|class=math.AT}}</ref> Precisely, it states that the suspension functor <math>\mathsf{nCat}_k \to \mathsf{nCat}_{k+1}</math> is an equivalence for <math>k \ge n + 2</math>.<ref>{{harvnb|Baez|Dolan|1995|loc=§ 5}}</ref>
